chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 75 — The Four Added Days and the Heavenly Doors
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. The surviving Aramaic manuscripts of the Astronomical Book from Qumran do not preserve wording corresponding to Chapter 75, and no extant Greek witness preserves it. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is therefore the translation base for all nine verses: the four added days, Uriel's oversight of the luminaries, the twelve solar doors, the windows and the heavenly chariots. Verse divisions follow the clauses of that Geʽez text; its statements about ancient calendrical and cosmic order are translated as given. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: The leaders of the heads of thousands, who are set over all creation and over all the stars, also serve with the four days that are added. They are not separated from their stations according to the complete reckoning of the year; these leaders serve on the four days that are not counted within the reckoning of the year.
verses.study: The four additional days belong to the leaders' appointed service and complete the calendar without dissolving its ordered stations. What appears outside the ordinary count still has a defined place.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — the heavenly lights mark days, seasons and years
Psalm 148:3–6 — the lights keep the decree appointed for them

verses.text: Because of these days people go astray in their reckoning. Yet those luminaries truly serve at the stations of the world: one at the first portal, one at the third portal, one at the fourth portal and one at the sixth portal. The exactness of the year is completed in its 364 distinct stations.
verses.study: Human miscalculation does not imply disorder in the lights themselves. The four stations complete the stated 364-day pattern with exactness.
crossReferences: Leviticus 23:4 — appointed times are to be proclaimed at their proper times
Daniel 2:21 — times and seasons remain under divine rule

verses.text: Uriel, the angel whom the Lord of Glory appointed forever over all the lights of heaven, showed me the signs, the appointed times, the years and the days. He was placed over them in heaven and in the world so that they might rule across the face of heaven, be seen upon the earth and lead the day and the night: the sun, the moon, the stars and all the ministering beings that circle in all the chariots of heaven.
verses.study: Uriel's instruction joins visible cycles to accountable oversight. The luminaries and their ministers serve an order established by the Lord of Glory.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:16–18 — the lights govern day and night
Psalm 19:1–6 — the sun's course bears witness across the earth

verses.text: In the same way Uriel showed me twelve open doors around the rim of the sun's chariot in heaven. Through them the rays of the sun go out, and from them heat goes out over the earth when they are opened at their appointed times.
verses.study: The twelve doors describe a measured distribution of sunlight and heat. Their opening at appointed times connects daily experience on earth with heavenly order.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 33:14 — the sun brings forth precious produce
Matthew 5:45 — the sun rises upon both evil and good

verses.text: They also open for the winds and for the breath of the dew at their appointed times, standing open in the heavens at the ends of the earth.
verses.study: Wind and dew are included beside heat within the ordered openings. The vision treats ordinary provisions of weather as appointed ministries.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:1 — God causes a wind to pass over the earth
Hosea 14:5 — the Lord's dew gives life and growth

verses.text: I saw twelve portals in heaven at the ends of the earth, from which the sun, the moon, the stars and all the works of heaven go out, from the east and from the west.
verses.study: The twelve portals encompass both east and west and gather the heavenly works into one ordered circuit. Rising and setting belong to a complete course.
crossReferences: Psalm 113:3 — praise extends from sunrise to sunset
Isaiah 45:6 — east and west are summoned to know the Lord

verses.text: Many windows stand open to their left and to their right. One window, at its appointed time, produces heat, like those doors from which the stars go out according to the command given them and in which they set according to their number.
verses.study: The windows operate by time, command and number. Each star's rising and setting is presented as faithful response rather than independent motion.
crossReferences: Job 38:31–33 — the constellations and ordinances of heaven are governed
Isaiah 40:26 — the stars are brought out and numbered

verses.text: I saw chariots in heaven racing through the world above and below those portals, in which the stars that never set make their circuit.
verses.study: The ceaseless stars move in chariots above and below the portals. Their motion widens the vision beyond the rising and setting bodies already described.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:9–10 — the heavenly throne is pictured with fiery wheels
Ezekiel 1:15–21 — heavenly wheels move under spiritual direction

verses.text: One of them is greater than all the others, and it circles the whole world.
verses.study: The chapter closes with the greatest circuit encompassing the world. Scale differs among the heavenly courses, but each belongs within the same ordered creation.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:6 — the sun's circuit reaches from one end of heaven to the other
Ecclesiastes 1:5 — the sun hastens back to the place of its rising

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 75 completes the 364-day reckoning by identifying four added days associated with leaders of the heavenly host. These days are distinct from the ordinary count yet essential to the year's exact completion.

The text locates the four days at the first, third, fourth and sixth portals. Human beings may err in calculating them, but the luminaries themselves continue to serve faithfully at their assigned stations.

Uriel's instruction then broadens from calendar reckoning to twelve doors around the sun's chariot. Heat, winds and dew pass through appointed openings, binding heavenly order to conditions experienced on earth.

The final vision includes eastern and western portals, neighboring windows and chariots bearing stars that do not set. Across differing movements, the chapter emphasizes command, number, appointed time and dependable service.

crossReferences: Genesis 1:14–18 — heavenly lights measure times and rule day and night
Job 38:31–33 — God governs constellations and heavenly ordinances
Psalm 19:1–6 — the sun completes its appointed course
Psalm 148:3–6 — sun, moon and stars keep an established decree
Isaiah 40:26 — the stars are brought out and numbered
Jeremiah 31:35 — fixed ordinances govern sun, moon and stars
